subject: Renewal planning: WAF/CDN (Cloudflare) + alternative options
messages:
From: Cloudflare ACCT Team <cf-renewals@cloudflare.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Cloudflare renewal notice and preliminary proposal

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well — our records show your current enterprise agreement for Cloudflare WAF + CDN is up for renewal on 2026-03-31. I’m attaching the preliminary renewal proposal (Cloudflare_Renewal_Proposal_Q1_2026.pdf) with tiered pricing that reflects the current traffic profile and the additional DDoS coverage you added in 2025.

High level: 12-month renewal, $X list, auto-SSL included, and an optional SOW for advanced bot mitigation and edge workers. Let me know if you want a formal PO path or an invoice.

Best,
Daniel Rossi
Enterprise Account Manager — Cloudflare

Attachment: Cloudflare_Renewal_Proposal_Q1_2026.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Cloudflare renewal notice and preliminary proposal

Forwarding Daniel’s note + proposal. Renewal window in Q1 — we need to decide if we renew Cloudflare as-is, negotiate price, or run a quick bake with Fastly/Akamai. Key asks:
- Cost delta if we keep current configuration vs. remove edge workers (CI)
- SLA and incident credit language (we had two incidents in 2025)
- Any migration effort if we evaluate alternatives (estimated ops hours)

Vivek — can you run a high-level ops estimate for switching WAF/CDN to a different provider (Fastly or Akamai) and a risk summary? Laura — want your view on commercial (discount levers, procurement timeline).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

--- Original message attached ---

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 14:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Cloudflare renewal notice and preliminary proposal

Marissa,

Quick ops estimate below — this is high level based on our 2025 traffic and the way we use Workers/KV:
- Fastly: ~4–6 weeks of engineering work to port VCL logic and edge-rules; expected migration runbook effort ~160–240 engineer-hours (including testing).
- Akamai: similar timeline but additional configuration for Kona WAF; expect extra effort for custom caching rules ~200–280 engineer-hours.
- Risk: TLS cert changes, cache hit-rate regression (performance hit for 1–2 weeks), geo-routing differences.
- Cost: vendor list pricing is comparable; discounting will matter. Cloudflare offers better X features for our current edge-worker usage.

I’ll attach WAF_usage_report_2025Q4.csv for your numbers. If we decide to chase cost aggressively, we should budget for a small POC with one service and a rollback plan.

-Vivek
Head of Infrastructure Security

Attachment: WAF_usage_report_2025Q4.csv

From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Cloudflare renewal notice and preliminary proposal

Team — thanks for the quick analysis. Procurement timeline and commercial levers:
- Procurement needs a final approved SOW/contract by 2026-03-01 to meet internal PO cutoff for the current fiscal quarter.
- We can ask for: 20–25% net on list (standard for us), extended SLA credits (financial), and a 90-day price lock for any added services.
- If Cloudflare won’t meet those terms we should request a competitive bid from Fastly/Akamai and run a short RFP (2 weeks for vendor responses + 2 weeks for technical POC).

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa — push Daniel for a redline-friendly term sheet and a consolidated quote that includes a separate line for Workers and for DDoS. Ask for committed capacity pricing.
2) Vivek — prepare a one-page migration risk/effort summary we can share with procurement and finance.
3) Stephanie — can you check budget approval timing and whether we can request an out-of-cycle exception if needed?

Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Operations

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
To: Cloudflare ACCT Team <cf-renewals@cloudflare.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 02 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cloudflare renewal notice and preliminary proposal

Hi Daniel — thanks for the proposal. A few items we need to clarify before moving forward:
- Can you provide a line-item quote separating CDN, WAF, Workers, and DDoS so we can map to internal budgets?
- Can Cloudflare confirm any incident credits for the two outages we experienced in 2025 (incidents logged under ticket #CF-2025-47 and #CF-2025-111)?
- Please include a one-page summary of the onboarding/migration effort if we were to split traffic and move only the WAF to another provider for testing.

We’d also like a redline-friendly contract or a draft SOW to circulate to Procurement — if you have a template we can push back on that speeds things up.

If possible, can you get this to us by 2026-02-09? We’re on a tight procurement schedule.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment requested: SOW template

From: Daniel Rossi <cf-renewals@cloudflare.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cloudflare renewal notice and preliminary proposal — updated proposal and SOW

Marissa / team — apologies for the short turnaround, attached the updated proposal and SOW (SOW_edge_migration_v2.docx). Key changes:
- Line-item pricing for CDN, WAF, Workers, DDoS.
- 22% net discount off list when committing to 12 months.
- Incident credits: offered 15% service credit for the two incidents in 2025, applied to first invoice.
- Migration support: 40 hours of engineering assistance for split-traffic POC, onboarding playbook included.

If that meets your needs we can provision a redline copy of the agreement for your procurement team and push a DocuSign link. If you still want competitive bids, we can pause while you evaluate; otherwise, we’ll hold pricing for 14 days from this email.

Regards,
Daniel Rossi
Enterprise Account Manager — Cloudflare

Attachments: SOW_edge_migration_v2.docx, Cloudflare_Renewal_Proposal_Q1_2026.pdf
